A vault is a folder whose files are encrypted. CryptBridge shows it as a drive letter — from your cloud (pCloud, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, MEGA) or from a folder on this PC or a USB drive.

How to get your own pCloud app (once; pCloud has to approve it)
  1. Open , log in with your pCloud account and request a new application.
  2. Fill in the request exactly like this, then click Create request:
    App nameCryptBridge (personal)
    Application TypePersonal use
    Folder accessAll folders — your vaults are normal folders in your pCloud
    Write accessYes — needed to upload files
    Websitehttps://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge
    Expected number of users1
    ReasonPersonal use only. I use the open-source tool CryptBridge (https://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge), which is based on rclone, to access my own pCloud account: it shows an encrypted folder of my pCloud as a drive on my own computers. Only my own pCloud account will use this app. It needs access to all folders because my existing encrypted folders are not inside an app folder, and write access to upload my files.
  3. Wait until pCloud approves the app. This can take a while — so request it now, before you need it.
  4. Open the approved app on My Apps and add this address under Redirect URIs:
    Without it, pCloud answers the sign-in with “redirect_uri is not authorized”.
  5. Copy the app's Client ID and Client secret into the fields below.
  6. Linux server (not urgent — its sign-in keeps working until pCloud blocks rclone's shared access again): create a new transfer block on the page of the vault, then on the server run sudo cryptbridge vault add (CryptBridge 0.9 or later; older servers: run the current setup.sh, see the README) and paste the block. The vault on the server takes the new sign-in.
How to set up your own Google app (once, about 15 minutes, free)
  1. Open the and sign in with your Google account. Create a new project, for example CryptBridge , and make sure it is selected at the top of the page.
  2. Turn on the : click Enable.
  3. Open the and click Get started:
    App nameCryptBridge (personal)
    User support emailyour own email address
    AudienceExternal
    Contact informationyour own email address; then agree and click Create
  4. Open , click Add or remove scopes and add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive (tick it in the list, or paste it under “Manually add scopes”). Click Update, then Save.
  5. Open , add your own Google address under Test users, then click Publish app and confirm. Important: while the app stays in “Testing”, Google ends every sign-in after 7 days. If Google asks for a homepage and a privacy policy first, enter them under Branding: https://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge . Done when “Publishing status” says In production. No verification needed: do not upload a logo and do not ask Google to check your branding. If Google still reports problems with the homepage or the privacy policy, ignore them.
  6. Open , click Create client, choose the application type Desktop app, name it CryptBridge and click Create.
  7. Copy the Client ID and the Client secret Google shows into the fields below. One Google app serves all your Google accounts.
  8. When you sign in, Google warns that it has not verified the app: it is your own app, which only you use. Click Advanced, then Go to CryptBridge (personal) (unsafe) and Continue.
How to set up your own Dropbox app (optional, about 5 minutes)
  1. Open the , sign in and click Create app: choose Scoped access and Full Dropbox, and give it a name of your own, for example “CryptBridge” followed by your name — Dropbox wants names that nobody else uses.
  2. On the Permissions tab, tick account_info.read, files.metadata.write, files.content.write, files.content.read and sharing.write, then click Submit.
  3. On the Settings tab, add this address under OAuth 2 Redirect URIs and click Add:
  4. Copy the App key into “Client ID” and the App secret into “Client secret” below.

The codes are stored encrypted with your Windows account, like your sign-in. They are not part of the transfer block: the server needs only the sign-in itself.

Linux server

Bring the sign-in to your cloud account and the keys of this vault to your server without typing them: create a transfer block, then run this command on the server and choose "Paste the transfer block".

curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/burnersen/CryptBridge/main/linux/setup.sh && sudo bash setup.sh
Transfer code (type it on the server when asked)
Transfer block

The block contains your keys, protected by the code. Never send block and code the same way (for example, not both in one e-mail). Block and code belong together: a new block gets a new code.

Emergency sheet

A page with everything needed to open this vault — even without CryptBridge. Print it and keep it like a house key. It is not saved anywhere by CryptBridge.

Remove from CryptBridge

CryptBridge forgets this vault and its keys. The files of the vault are not touched — with the emergency sheet you can add it again at any time.

    Appearance

    Cache

    Files copied to a drive are first stored here. For cloud vaults, recently used files stay here too, so that films start fast. Shared by all drives.

    The cache can only be changed while all drives are disconnected. Files that are still waiting for upload stay in the old cache folder — finish uploads before you move it. The cache holds files decrypted; with the app lock on, it is deleted whenever CryptBridge locks.

    Behaviour

    Whether a drive connects when CryptBridge starts is set for each vault on its page.

    App lock — recommended

    With an app password, CryptBridge starts locked and locks itself again when you lock Windows (Win+L) or sign out. Locked, the drives are closed (after running uploads are done), rclone is stopped, and the cache with readable copies of your files is deleted. The cloud sign-ins and the vault keys are stored sealed with the app password. The emergency sheets and the transfer block ask for it, too.

    The app password is not a vault password: if you forget it, your files are not lost — you set CryptBridge up again with the emergency sheets.

    State
    Off
    Change the app password
    Turn the app lock off

    LAN access — optional

    Lets the other devices of your home network open the connected drives over WebDAV: a TV or Apple TV with a video player such as Infuse or Kodi, a phone, a tablet, a Mac. Every connected drive appears there as a folder. The files travel through your home network decrypted, protected by user name and password; devices outside your home network cannot reach them. Locking CryptBridge ends the LAN access at once.

    There are two accesses, each with a port, user name and password of its own. Give TVs and video players the streaming access, and use the full access only on devices you trust.

    Streaming access (read only)

    For TVs and video players: they can open, play and copy files, but cannot change or delete anything.

    State
    Off
    Address for your devices

    Full access (read and write)

    For file apps on a phone, a tablet or a Mac: they can also upload, rename and delete. Such files go into the drive's upload queue like files copied in Explorer. Its password must differ from the streaming password.

    State
    Off
    Address for your devices
    Windows firewall
    —
    Tips for your devices
    • Video players (Infuse, Kodi) and file apps: add a WebDAV share with the address of the access (protocol http, its port, path /), its user name and its password.
    • Mac: Finder → Go → Connect to Server, enter the address.
    • Other Windows PCs refuse a password-protected http:// WebDAV address unless their registry is changed — install CryptBridge there instead.
    • While this PC sleeps or is switched off, the drives cannot be reached from the network.
    • Windows lets devices in only on networks it counts as private (home networks), never on public ones such as a hotel or café network.
